title: Infinitesimal unipotent invariants in restricted induced modules
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that iterated commutator subgroup schemes become trivial, and finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with unipotent radical $U$, projection $\pi_T:B\to T$, character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, and coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. A split torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup, and the unipotent radical is the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Put $Q=S/B$ and $N=|\Phi^+|$. For $\mu\in X$ let $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\mu\circ\pi_T}$ be the homogeneous invertible sheaf for the action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\mu(\pi_T(b))z)$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections]. Let $w_0$ be the longest Weyl element [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit]. Let $\lambda\in X$ satisfy $0\le\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle<p$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$. Put $V(\lambda)=\Gamma(Q,M_{-w_0\lambda})$ with left translation $(g f)(s)=f(g^{-1}s)$ in the semi-invariant-function realization [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections]. For $x\in\mathfrak u=\operatorname{Lie}(U)$ let $xv$ be the differentiated action on $V(\lambda)$. Then $V(\lambda)$ is finite-dimensional and there is $0\ne v_\lambda\in V(\lambda)$ such that
$$\{v\in V(\lambda):xv=0\text{ for all }x\in\mathfrak u\}=Fv_\lambda.$$
The group $U$ fixes $v_\lambda$ and $T$ acts on its line with character $\lambda$. This is an assertion about Lie-algebra invariants, not merely $U(F)$-fixed vectors. The case $S=1$, $\lambda=0$ is included.

proof.text: Apply the dual induced-module presentation with $\eta=\lambda$. It gives $0\ne V=V(\lambda)$ finite-dimensional and $W=V^\vee=Hw$, with $D_i^{(b)}w=0$ for $b>m_i=\langle\lambda,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle$. The section comparison identifies $V$ with $E_B(w_0\lambda\circ\pi_T)$. Apply the primitive-line lemma to this nonzero module: its $U$-fixed line is $Fv_\lambda\ne0$, of character $w_0(w_0\lambda)=\lambda$, since $w_0^2=1$. These are group-scheme fixed vectors and characters.

source.place: Lemma 2.3, proof, printed p.155; dualization and conventions from Lemma 2.1, pp.153--154. Online source read; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Use the distribution calculus and its infinitesimal subalgebra $A\subseteq H$. Set $Z=Aw\subseteq W$. For $a\in A$, its identity gives $D_i^{(n)}aw=\sum_{r+b=n}C_{i,r}(a)D_i^{(b)}w$. Terms with $b\ge p$ vanish because $m_i<p$. For $b<p$, $D_i^{(b)}\in A$, and $C_{i,r}(a)\in A$, so every remaining term belongs to $Aw$. Thus $Z$ is stable under every $D_i^{(n)}$. These generate $H$, whence $Hw\subseteq Z$; the reverse inclusion follows from $A\subseteq H$. Consequently $W=Aw$. This proves the restricted cyclicity here, rather than assuming Lie invariants coincide with group invariants.

source.place: Lemma 2.3, proof, printed p.155; dualization and conventions from Lemma 2.1, pp.153--154. Online source read; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $L=\mathfrak uW$ denote the span of all $x\ell$, $x\in\mathfrak u$, $\ell\in W$. As $A$ is generated by $1$ and $\mathfrak u$, $W=Aw$ is spanned by $w$ and positive-length words $x_1\cdots x_kw$. Every such word lies in $L$, so $W/L$ is spanned by the class of $w$. Differentiate the contragredient identity: $(x\ell)(v)=-\ell(xv)$. Thus for a Lie-invariant $v$, the functional $\ell\mapsto\ell(v)$ annihilates $L$ and is determined by its value at $w$. Conversely this annihilation implies $xv=0$, since linear functionals separate vectors. Evaluation is injective into $W^*$, so the space of Lie invariants has dimension at most one. Differentiating the group-fixed identity for the nonzero $v_\lambda$ of step 1 gives $xv_\lambda=0$ for every $x\in\mathfrak u$. Hence the invariant space is exactly $Fv_\lambda$, with the asserted $U$-fixity and $T$-character from step 1. For $S=1$, $H=A=F$ and the same argument gives $V=F$, including $\lambda=0$.
